source.buildings: OpenStreetMap building footprints (way/relation[building]) via the Overpass API, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; plus Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (India, release 2026-02-03, ODbL) wherever a Microsoft footprint's centroid is not inside an OSM footprint. Class from the OSM building tag (commercial/public, industrial, else residential); untyped and Microsoft buildings inside landuse=commercial/retail or industrial take that class. Assigned to the cell holding the footprint centroid; footprints larger than half a cell are spread over the cells whose centres they cover, and no cell holds more footprint than its own area (overlaps scaled down).
source.roads: OpenStreetMap road centrelines (highway motorway..service, bridges and tunnels left out) via the Overpass API, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Surface = length × a width per road class (placeholder_needs_calibration: typical carriageway widths chosen by the tool, not measured).
source.agriculture: CZMP khazan mask (the CRZ grid), plus OSM landuse=farmland/paddy polygons by cell centre.
source.censusUnits: DataMeet Indian village boundaries, Goa (github.com/datameet/indian_village_boundaries, ODbL), 2001 census codes; each cell takes the unit holding its centre.

encoding: sparse: flat [cell index, value] pairs for non-zero cells (row-major index on the panjimCrzGrid.json grid); divide the value by the scale
grounding_note: OSM footprints are volunteered and incomplete in Panjim; Microsoft's machine-learned footprints fill most gaps but can miss or merge buildings in dense blocks and carry no use class. A building missing from both carries no damage. Building class from tags is coarse (most Panjim buildings are tagged only building=yes, so they count as residential unless they sit in a commercial or industrial landuse polygon).
